title: Zion! the City of Our God
description: Zion! the City of Our God in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book II, hymn 24, “Asking the way to Zion. Jer 1:5”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Zi-on! the cit-y of our God, How glo-rious is the place! The Sa-vior there has his a-bode, And sin-ners see his face.

lines: Zion! the city of our God,
The Savior there has his abode,
There, all the fruits of glory grow,
And streams of grace, and knowledge flow,
And let a union to the Lord
The gospel shines to give you light,
The Spirit waits to guide you right,
O Lord, regard thy peoples prayer,
And young and old, by grace prepare,

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
